questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had exciting geography courses and was close to mountains, so I could go skiing and hiking.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: An amazing experience. The university is great, and Banff and Jasper are very easily accessible and offer great adventures. However, the city itself is a bit boring.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some information was easy to find; however, it was a bit difficult. They have an international student service where a lot of the information can be found, and they also had a zoom meeting. However, what was needed for immigration was not always clear, and to get housing on campus, you needed to be fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a welcome center where I could ask all my questions. They also have an orientation event for all exchange students. You can always ask them questions, and they organize events throughout the whole term.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They answered quickly; however, it was a bit confusing since much of the information was for international students as well, and therefore you got told a lot of things that do not apply to exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can choose between 1, 2, 3 or 4-bedroom apartments on campus

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were available. I did not choose one. It was almost 50/50 among the exchange students, so half of the people cooked by themselves and the other half used the meal plan. In the apartment, you have a kitchen, but you need to buy everything yourself since it is not equipped with anything.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is a great way to meet people and is very convenient, especially when it gets cold outside. So I will recommend it. It can be recommended to go somewhere cheap and buy all you need since the apartment does not have anything when you arrive, so you need to buy bedding. If the apartment is damaged when you get there, then make a maintenance request, and they will fix it for free.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was expensive, considering how old it is, and it is annoying that you need to buy everything yourself just to sell it or throw it out four months later. I recommend people to live off campus, but you need to be fast with the application since it is quickly filling up.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty straightforward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You select the courses you want online on their version of KUNET, and then you are enrolled in them and can see your timetable immediately. However, information about the courses is scarce, so it is hard to know, for example, what kind of exam a course has before you select it. If you want courses higher than the first year, you probably need to be approved for them in advance, which is not difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office and international student service could guide and help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up the professors and try something you cannot do at home. Also, try a lot of different courses in the beginning and remove the ones you do not like. You have the first two weeks to try courses and drop them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was a bit lower than at home, but they grade you throughout the term, and presentations and assignments all count towards your final grade, which can be a bit stressful. Therefore the workload was also a bit more than what I am used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was easier than back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had midterms, assignments and presentations, which they graded me on. My classes were mostly lectures with additional group work, similar to what I am used to at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOG 480 - Cartography and Geovisualization
DEST 402 - Global Food Politics
DEST 405 - Environment and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had very nice professors in all my courses, so I can recommend all of them. I especially found Environment and Development very interesting since we were discussing solutions to solve global warming.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Personal spending also covers trips to Banff and Jasper here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive, but books were less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs you could join, and with the mountains so close, there were endless possibilities to have fun every weekend.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were clubs for almost everything, so you could find something that definitely fits your interest.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go skiing and hiking in Banff and Jasper as much as possible. Go skating, go to an ice hockey match and go running.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As already said, go to Banff and Jasper and hike or ski. Vancouver is also definitely worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since it is almost the same culture as in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the events in the beginning and talk to people in your class. Also, choose to have a roommate so you can socialize at home.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are very friendly and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live on campus and take courses that are different than at home.
Go hiking and skiing every weekend in the Rockies. It is worth the money and why many people come to UofC.
Be social and seek help if you need it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, but remember that you are only there for a short time so use all the time you have because it will be over before you know it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To speak in front of the entire class at presentations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it because it is worth every second:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
